'''Catherine Greenhill''' {{Post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA|FRSN}} is an Australian pure mathematician known for her research on [[random graph]]s, [[combinatorial enumeration]] and [[Markov chain]]s.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |last=Greenhill |first=Catherine |title=Catherine Greenhill {{!}} Biography |url=https://web.maths.unsw.edu.au/~csg/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250601094546/https://web.maths.unsw.edu.au/~csg/ |archive-date=1 June 2025 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=web.maths.unsw.edu.au |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> She is a professor of mathematics in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of New South Wales]].<ref name="bio" />

== Education ==
Greenhill was born in [[Queensland|Queensland, Australia]]. She attended [[St Margaret's Anglican Girls' School]], where she developed an interest in mathematics and science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Catherine Greenhill - St Margaret's |url=https://www.stmargarets.qld.edu.au/125/125-notables/catherine-greenhill |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=www.stmargarets.qld.edu.au |archive-date=14 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114080008/https://www.stmargarets.qld.edu.au/125/125-notables/catherine-greenhill |url-status=live }}</ref> She then completed a Bachelor of Science (Hons) at the [[University of Queensland]] in 1991, followed by a Master of Science by research in 1992, supervised by [[Anne Penfold Street]]. She earned her Ph.D. in 1996 at the [[University of Oxford]], under the supervision of [[Peter M. Neumann]].<ref name="bio" /> Her dissertation was ''From Multisets to Matrix Groups: Some Algorithms Related to the Exterior Square''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|46105}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing her PhD, she obtained a postdoctoral position at the [[University of Leeds]] where she worked on the analysis of combinatorial [[Markov chain|Markov chains]] and its [[computational complexity]].<ref name="bio" /> She then moved back to Australia where she took up an [[Australian Research Council]] postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of Melbourne]], working with [[Nick Wormald]] on the study of [[Random regular graph|random regular graphs]].<ref name="bio" />

In 2003, she joined the [[University of New South Wales]] (UNSW) and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2014, the first female mathematician to earn such a promotion at UNSW.<ref name="heyde" /> In 2019, she was one of the first three female mathematicians to be promoted to Professor at UNSW.<ref>{{Cite web |title=School Staff promoted to Professor |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/news/2018/11/school-staff-promoted-to-professor |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=UNSW Sites |language=en |archive-date=23 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260123103855/https://www.unsw.edu.au/news/2018/11/school-staff-promoted-to-professor |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, she was appointed Head of the Pure Mathematics Department at UNSW.<ref name="bio" /> She is currently the head of the [[Combinatorics]] group in the School of Mathematics at UNSW.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Professor Catherine Greenhill |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/staff/catherine-greenhill |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=UNSW Sites |language=en |archive-date=23 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240423191344/https://www.unsw.edu.au/staff/catherine-greenhill |url-status=live }}</ref> Her main research interests lie in asymptotic, probabilistic and algorithmic combinatorics.<ref name=":0" />

She is a former editor-in-chief of the ''[[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]],''<ref name="ejc">{{Cite web |title=Editorial Team {{!}} The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics |url=https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/about/editorialTeam |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102181019/https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/about/editorialTeam |archive-date=2026-01-02 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=www.combinatorics.org |language=en-US}}</ref> a member of the editorial board for ''Random Structures & Algorithms''<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10982418/homepage/editorialboard.html |title=Random Structures & Algorithms |publisher=Wiley |language=en |doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1098-2418 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430173452/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10982418/homepage/editorialboard.html |archive-date=2024-04-30}}</ref> and the ''[[Australasian Journal of Combinatorics]],''<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Australasian Journal of Combinatorics |url=http://ajc.maths.uq.edu.au/?page=editorial_team |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101005237/http://ajc.maths.uq.edu.au/?page=editorial_team |archive-date=2026-01-01 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=ajc.maths.uq.edu.au |language=en}}</ref> and a member of the editorial advisory board for ''Special Matrices.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last= |title=Catherine Greenhill Leadership, service etc the School of Mathematics and Statistics at UNSW.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Catherine Greenhill |url=https://research.unsw.edu.au/people/professor-catherine-greenhill |archive-date=2025-11-07 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=Simon Marais Mathematics Competition |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==

* In 2010, she received the Hall Medal of the [[Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=The ICA Medals |url=https://luca-giuzzi.unibs.it/ICA/medals.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250903121757/https://luca-giuzzi.unibs.it/ICA/medals.php |archive-date=2025-09-03 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=The [[Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications]] |language=en}}</ref>
* In 2013, she was awarded the UNSW Faculty of Science June Griffith Fellowship for Academic Women in Leadership.<ref name="heyde" />
* In 2015, she received the Christopher Heyde Medal from the [[Australian Academy of Science]] for distinguished research in the mathematical sciences.<ref name="heyde">{{Cite web |title=Catherine Greenhill wins Australian Academy of Science 2015 Christopher Heyde Medal |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/news/2014/11/catherine-greenhill-wins-australian-academy-of-science-2015-chri |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=UNSW Sites |language=en |archive-date=16 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116121301/https://www.unsw.edu.au/news/2014/11/catherine-greenhill-wins-australian-academy-of-science-2015-chri |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2022, she was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-26 |title=Academy announces 2022 Fellows for outstanding contributions to science |url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/two-firsts-academy-announces-2022-fellows |access-date=2022-05-25 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en |archive-date=26 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326235248/https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/two-firsts-academy-announces-2022-fellows |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2023, she was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Catherine Greenhill, Fellow (2023) : Sydney |url=https://www.royalsoc.org.au/fellows/catherine-greenhill-fellow-2023-sydney/ |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=The Royal Society of NSW |language=en-US}}</ref>
